articles.content:
July 9, 2026

More intelligence from every token, stronger performance per dollar, and more capability on demand for your hardest work.

Learn about OpenAI’s latest model:

Update on August 21, 2026:OpenAI dropped the API and credit pricing of GPT‑5.6 Sol by over 20% for the next 3 months.

Update on July 30, 2026:OpenAI reduced the price of GPT‑5.6 Luna by 80% and GPT‑5.6 Terra by 20%.Learn more here.

We’re launching the GPT‑5.6 family of models for general availability following ourlimited preview⁠: our new flagship,Sol, alongsideTerra, a balanced model for everyday work, andLuna, our most cost-efficient model.

GPT‑5.6 Sol sets a new standard for both intelligence and efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art results across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and science while outperforming previous and competing frontier models with fewer tokens and at lower estimated cost. The result is stronger performance per dollar: more successful work for the same spend, or comparable results at a lower total cost. We also introduce a new way to accelerate the most demanding work:ultrais our highest-capability setting, coordinating multiple agents across parallel workstreams to finish complex tasks faster. Stronger computer use and design judgment make GPT‑5.6 Sol our most polished collaborator yet, helping it inspect, refine, and deliver ready-to-use results.

We trained GPT‑5.6 to get more useful work from every token. OnAgents’ Last Exam⁠(opens in a new window), an evaluation of long-running professional workflows across 55 fields, GPT‑5.6 Sol sets a new high of 53.6, eclipsing Claude Fable 5 (adaptive reasoning) by 13.1 points. Even at medium reasoning, it beats Fable 5 by 11.4 points at roughly one-quarter the estimated cost. That efficiency extends to smaller models, which are essential to making intelligence more abundant and affordable: GPT‑5.6 Terra and GPT‑5.6 Luna outperform Fable 5 at around one-sixteenth the cost. On theArtificial Analysis Intelligence Index⁠(opens in a new window), a broad measure of intelligence spanning agentic work, coding, scientific reasoning, and general capabilities, GPT‑5.6 Sol with max reasoning comes within one point of Fable 5 while completing tasks in 61% less time at roughly half the estimated cost.

GPT‑5.6 launches with our most robust safeguards to date, designed to be resilient against determined and adaptive misuse without broadly limiting legitimate work. Before general availability, we put the models and safeguards through our most extensive evaluation period yet, combining human red teaming with large-scale automated testing. During the preview, we worked closely with expert organizations and with trusted partners to pressure-test defenses and strengthen safeguards before broader launch. The resulting system layers protections trained into the model with real-time checks, monitoring, and access calibrated to trust and risk.

GPT‑5.6 Sol is our best coding model yet. On theArtificial Analysis Coding Agent Index,GPT‑5.6 Sol with max reasoning sets a new state of the art at 80, 2.8 points above Fable 5, while using less than half the output tokens, taking less than half the time, and costing about one-third less. That advantage extends across the family: Terra performs just above Fable 5, while Luna outperforms Opus 4.8; each does so in roughly one-third of the time, with about half as many output tokens, and at approximately one-quarter the estimated cost. It also sets new state-of-the-art results on Terminal‑Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE, which test complex command-line workflows and long-horizon engineering in real codebases.

GPT‑5.6 can write and run lightweight programs that coordinate tools, process intermediate results, monitor progress, and choose the next action as work unfolds. This lets tool-heavy tasks advance with fewer tokens, fewer model round trips, and less guidance. Instead of requiring developers to script every step or passing every tool response back through the model,Programmatic Tool Calling⁠(opens in a new window)in the Responses API can filter large amounts of intermediate data, retain only what matters, and adapt its workflow along the way.

For problems that reward a greater investment of time and compute, GPT‑5.6 can push beyond this efficient default.maxgives GPT‑5.6 even more time thanxhighto reason and explore alternatives, run checks, and revise its approach.ultragoes further by coordinating four agents in parallel by default, trading higher token use for stronger results and faster time-to-result on demanding tasks. The charts below compare ultra’s default four-agent setup with a one-agent baseline across BrowseComp, SEC-Bench Pro, and Terminal-Bench 2.1; BrowseComp and SEC-Bench Pro also show 16-agent configurations. Across all three evaluations, adding parallel agents shifts the score-latency frontier upward and to the left, reaching stronger results in less time. In the API, developers can build ultra-like experiences using themulti-agent⁠(opens in a new window)beta in the Responses API.4,5,6

GPT‑5.6 delivers a step change in design judgment. With only high-level direction, GPT‑5.6 creates tasteful, ergonomic, and functional interfaces. Its stronger computer-use capabilities let it inspect and refine the rendered result—not just generate the underlying code or content—so it can catch visual and functional issues and apply finishing touches before handing the work back.

GPT‑5.6’s frontend capabilities also turn natural-language requests into polished, interactive explanations and visualizations within ChatGPT Work.

GPT‑5.6delivers better results for professional tasks. It takes messy context from your documents and everyday workflows like Slack, Notion, Microsoft 365, and Google Drive, and converts it into expert-level, shareable artifacts.

GPT‑5.6’s strength on knowledge work shows up in evaluations spanning long-horizon professional analysis, browsing, tool use, and computer use. GPT‑5.6 Sol sets new state-of-the-art results onBrowseCompat 92.2% andOSWorld 2.0at 62.6%; on OSWorld, it surpasses Opus 4.8 while using 85% fewer output tokens. Here, the performance-per-dollar gains extend across the GPT‑5.6 family. Luna nearly matches GPT‑5.5’s peak performance at less than half the estimated cost, while Terra surpasses it at a lower cost.

GPT‑5.6 Sol improves quality in presentations, documents, and spreadsheets,producing outputs that are more polished and accurate. It can create fully editable presentations from scratch, translating a prompt and source material into a coherent visual narrative with strong layouts, hierarchy, and design.

The improvement is especially pronounced when following templates and reference decks.GPT‑5.6 can infer a deck’s design system—layouts, typography, spacing, colors, and recurring content patterns, including rules embedded in the Slide Master—and apply those conventions consistently to new material. In this example, when asked to update numbers based on a reference file, the GPT‑5.5 output is missing key components from the master slide, while GPT‑5.6 follows the reference structure more faithfully.

GPT‑5.6 also creates more visually refined documents and spreadsheets. It follows complex reference formats more faithfully, which is important for repeatable knowledge work activities. It handles equations and financial models with greater precision, and makes better use of typography, spacing, hierarchy, and page or worksheet layout.

Early customers testing GPT‑5.6 saw improvements to knowledge work outputs across domains.

GPT‑5.6 is our strongest cybersecurity model yet, achieving frontier performance with significantly fewer tokens. OnExploitBench2,which measures progress from reaching vulnerable code through arbitrary code execution, it scores 73.5% versus GPT‑5.5’s 47.9% at a comparable output-token budget. OnExploitGym3,which asks agents to turn real-world vulnerabilities into working exploits, it almost doubles GPT‑5.5’s peak pass rate, from 15.1% to 24.9% under the two-hour cap; with six hours, it reaches 33.7%. OnSEC-Bench Pro,which tests proof-of-concept generation on complex software, it scores 71.2% versus GPT‑5.5’s 45.8% at an improved latency.1

GPT‑5.6 supports important defensive tasks such as secure code review, patching, threat modeling, and blue teaming. Qualified individuals and organizations inOpenAI Daybreak’s Trusted Access for Cyber⁠program can access more of its defensive capability through more precise safeguards for verified work in authorized environments, including vulnerability triage and validation, malware analysis, detection engineering, and patch validation.

Users who do not already have hardware-backed passkeys can receivepreferred pricing⁠(opens in a new window)from our partner, Yubico. We are also taking additional steps to restrict access to high-risk entities and in high-risk jurisdictions.

GPT‑5.6 Sol also shows broad gains acrossscientific research. On life sciences evaluations, GPT‑5.6 demonstrates Pareto improvements over GPT‑5.5 on real-world biology, life science research workflows, and chemistry.

GPT‑5.6 is our strongest model yet for accelerating AI research. Inside OpenAI, researchers use it across the development loop: diagnosing failures, optimizing training systems, running experiments, and interpreting results. We already saw that acceleration and stronger adoption during the internal testing period of GPT‑5.6, as average daily output tokens per active researcher were more than twice the highest level observed for GPT‑5.5.

articles.title: Meta Releases Muse Spark Open: 816B Open-Weight MoE With 1M Context
articles.content: Meta Superintelligence Labs has released Muse Spark Open, the open-weight version of its Muse Spark model. Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates 42B parameters per token. It takes text, image, video and audio input, returns text, and holds a 1M-token context window. Meta team claims it to be the most capable US open-weight model to date. For developers, the real news is deployment: the NVFP4 build runs on 2 Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. TL;DR Size: 816B total / 42B active parameters (256 experts, 8 active per token); 1M-token context. Runs on: 2 Mac Studios (M5 Ultra, 512 GB each) via MLX; 4 Blackwell Ultra GPUs or 8 H200s with NVFP4; about 300 GB setups via Unsloth 2-bit GGUF. Performance: Strong on agentic tool use; mid-pack among large open models on coding. Best: MCP-Atlas 89.2, the top score in Meta’s comparison table. Worst: Terminal-Bench 2.1 76.4, behind Kimi K3 (85.0), GLM 5.3 (83.9) and Qwen3.8 (82.0). What is Muse Spark Open? Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal MoE model from Meta, built for coding and long-horizon agentic work. Weights ship in BF16 and NVFP4 on Hugging Face. The open version received extra safety post-training. Meta team states that this makes it more robust without system-level guardrails. How does the architecture work? The model card lists 62 layers and a hidden dimension of 8192. Each MoE layer holds 256 experts, and top-k routing activates 8 per token. Attention is grouped-query, with 128 query heads and 16 KV heads. A separate 1.8B-parameter Perception Encoder handles visual input. The vocabulary has 202,048 tokens, and training data covers more than 100 languages. Reasoning depth is set with reasoning_effort: low, medium, high or xhigh. The default is xhigh. How does Muse Spark Open perform on benchmarks? Meta compares it with Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and others at maximum reasoning effort. Its strongest results are on tool use and knowledge reliability: MCP-Atlas: 89.2, ahead of Qwen3.8 (84.5) and GLM 5.3 (84.2). JobBench: 61.8, narrowly ahead of GLM 5.3 (61.4). HLE-Diamond, no tools: 26.1, versus 22.2 for Kimi K3. AA Omniscience: 25, the top score in Meta’s table. ZeroBench with tools: 50.0, versus 41.0 for Kimi K3. Coding is the weak spot. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 with the Terminus 2 harness, it scores 76.4. Kimi K3 reaches 85.0, GLM 5.3 scores 83.9 and Qwen3.8 scores 82.0. Its Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is 39. That sits behind GLM 5.3 (45), Kimi K3 (44) and Qwen3.8 (40). So “most capable US” holds, but Chinese open models still lead overall. Some rival scores are self-reported; the evaluation methodology lists each source. && What hardware does Muse Spark Open need? Per Meta’s developer guide, BF16 weights are about 1.6 TB. NVFP4 quantizes only the experts and lands near 530 GB. The model card recommends at least 700 GB of VRAM for NVFP4 and 2 TB for BF16. Data center: NVFP4 on 4 Blackwell Ultra GPUs or 8 H200s. Desktop: 2 M5 Ultra Mac Studios with 512 GB each, linked over Thunderbolt 5 with RDMA. MLX tensor parallelism splits every layer across both machines. Workstation: Unsloth Dynamic GGUFs down to 2-bit fit in about 300 GB of combined memory. Where can developers run it? Day-one engines include SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, MLX, llama.cpp and Unsloth. Hosted APIs are live on Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. OpenRouter lists $1.25 per 1M input tokens and $4.25 per 1M output tokens. Two draft models speed up decoding: DFlash V2 for SGLang and DSpark for vLLM. Meta reports 3.7x single-request throughput with DFlash V2 on AMD MI355X. Fine-tuning works with TorchTitan, Hugging Face TRL and NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel. What does the Muse Model License allow? The Muse Model License permits use, fine-tuning, distillation and redistribution. 2 conditions matter most: Products must display “Built with Muse Spark Open.” Model-as-a-Service providers above $20M in 12-month revenue need a separate agreement with Meta. Internal use, research and powering your own product features are exempt from the revenue clause. Free for most; MaaS providers above $20M revenue need a deal. Check out the model weights, research blog, developer guide and evaluation methodology. Meta 비교표에서는 도구 사용 성능이 강점인 반면 일부 코딩 평가에서는 경쟁 모델보다 낮아, 전 영역의 우위로 해석하기는 어렵다.

articles.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B Open Multimodal Agent Model
articles.content: NVIDIA just released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open vision-language model built for always-on enterprise agents. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model from NVIDIA that activates 12B parameters per token. It reads text, images, documents and video, then reasons, calls tools and writes code in one model. For developers, 1 open checkpoint replaces a separate text model along with a separate vision model. NVIDIA also shipped 2 edge models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Bolt E4B. TL;DR Size: 120B total parameters, 12B active (MoE). Context up to 1M tokens. Runs on: 1x DGX Spark, 1x H200, 2x H100 or 1x GB200 with the NVFP4 checkpoint. A BF16 checkpoint is also published. Performance: Strong reasoning, agentic coding and document vision. NVIDIA claims up to 5x higher single-GPU throughput than open peers. Best: 89.90 on GPQA-Diamond (NVFP4). Worst: 17.78 on tau3-bench banking (NVFP4). What is Nemotron 3.5 Super VL? It is an open multimodal agent model. Weights ship under the OpenMDW-1.1 license. NVIDIA also released open datasets, training recipes and RL environments in NeMo Gym. The model card lists text, image and video inputs with text output. Video is limited to MP4 clips up to 2 minutes. Reasoning can be toggled on or off through the chat template. How does the architecture work? The backbone interleaves Mamba-2, mixture-of-experts and attention layers. Each MoE layer holds 512 routed experts. A C-RADIO vision encoder and a connector feed images, document pages and video frames into the language backbone. Speed comes from four techniques: Multi-token prediction: a native drafter proposes several tokens, verified in 1 forward pass. LiLiCorr: a speculative drafter for DGX Spark, up to 2.3x faster token generation. NVFP4 with quantization-aware distillation: 4-bit weights and activations on Blackwell, 4-bit weights with 16-bit activations elsewhere. Context reuse: prefix caching keeps both attention caches and Mamba states across agent turns. The model was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra. NVIDIA team states that it trained on about 26 trillion tokens. Post-training used roughly 3.8 million samples plus RL across dozens of environments. Continued pretraining added 10B Indic tokens. How does it perform on benchmarks? All scores below are NVIDIA-reported, from the NVFP4 checkpoint on the model card. articles.title: Perplexity Open-Sources SPACE, a Firecracker MicroVM Sandbox for AI Agents
articles.content: Perplexity has open-sourced SPACE, the sandbox platform behind every task in Perplexity Computer. The Perplexity SPACE sandbox gives each agent task its own Firecracker microVM. Credentials and outbound traffic are controlled from outside that VM. The code ships under Apache 2.0 on GitHub. For teams building coding or browsing agents, this is a production-tested isolation layer they can self-host. TL;DR Size: Rust codebase, release 0.8.0, the public baseline. HTTP API plus server-sent events. Runs on: A Linux x86_64 host with KVM, /dev/kvm, btrfs and Docker. Local Kind (Kubernetes) or direct mode. No macOS. Performance: In production, median create latency fell from 185 ms to 60 ms versus Perplexity’s previous provider. Best: 0 of 108 VM-to-host escape attempts succeeded across 9 frontier models. Worst: Before fixes, agents bypassed the egress policy in 11 of 54 partial-network runs. What is Perplexity SPACE? SPACE (Sandboxed Platform for Agentic Code Execution) is Perplexity’s platform for running agent code in isolated microVMs. Applications call its HTTP API to create Linux environments, run commands and stream output. A template supplies the starting filesystem. A sandbox is one instance of that template, with its own VM and writable disk. Many commands can run inside one sandbox. Perplexity’s launch thread explains the design goal. Agents run commands, install packages and call services with root inside the sandbox. The host stays outside the guest’s control. Agent work is long-running, stateful and branching, so it must survive restarts. How does SPACE isolate agents? Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM with its own guest kernel. A per-sandbox network gateway on the host enforces egress policy on every outbound connection. Secrets never enter the guest. Per Perplexity’s July engineering post, credentials are injected at the network layer. The credential store adds hierarchical scoping, rate limits and audit logging. The architecture guide splits the system into 4 parts. These are a PostgreSQL-backed API, controllers, worker services and a data plane. Worker services manage VMs, networking, volumes, templates and credentials. btrfs copy-on-write creates each root filesystem. How do pause, suspend and restore work? Sandboxes move through 4 states: running, paused, suspended and deleted. Paused: VM memory stays resident on the worker. This is not a durable snapshot. Suspended: VM memory, runtime state and root filesystem are snapshotted. Active resources are released. Idle default: sandboxes suspend after 6 hours without activity. For fast creates, Kubernetes deployments use warm pools of booted sandboxes. Single-node setups use base snapshots instead. In production, the 90th-percentile create latency dropped from 447 ms to 89 ms. Perplexity reports that 100% of Computer sessions run on SPACE. Did SPACE survive a red-team test? Perplexity’s Escaping SPACE: Part I report tested 9 models with root inside the guest. The study ran 216 runs across 2 tasks and 4 settings. Sandbox escape: 0 of 108 runs reached the host-side secret. No-network bypass: 0 of 54 runs succeeded. Partial-network bypass: 11 of 54 runs succeeded before fixes. 4 models found a path. Claude Opus 5.0, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Cyber and Kimi K3 found bypasses. The attacks used DNS spoofing and shared CDN IP addresses. Perplexity then added source-address validation through nftables. The gateway now terminates TLS and checks both SNI and HTTP host against the allowlist. In the retest, no model produced a verified bypass. The same team tested 10 third-party platforms. 8 showed at least one network-policy bypass. Perplexity disclosed the results to every affected vendor. articles.title: Liquid AI Releases d1-ultra: A Multimodal Decision Model That Scores 65 on the AA Decision Index
articles.content: Liquid AI has released d1-ultra, its most capable decision model to date. The Liquid AI d1-ultra decision model reads text, images, or both. It answers typed questions with a probability for each possible answer. It does this in one forward pass and generates no output tokens. For developers, that means classification, routing and scoring calls without paying for generated text. It is available now on the Liquid API at $0.042 per million input tokens. TL;DR Size: Parameters and context length not disclosed. Built on a larger open-weight backbone than d1. Runs on: Hosted Liquid API only. No downloadable weights or quantized variants announced. Performance: Leads all 8 categories in Liquid’s 112-evaluation suite, per Liquid. Best: 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index, ranked #1 (Liquid-reported). Worst: No public per-benchmark breakdown or parameter count yet; claims are vendor-reported. What is a decision model? A decision model answers bounded questions with probabilities instead of free text. Liquid’s decision model docs describe 3 question types: Noul: a yes/no question that returns a probability between 0 and 1. Choice: one label from a set, with a probability per label. Score: a probability-weighted position on an ordered rubric. The docs recommend decision models for routing, moderation, guardrails, triage and LLM-as-judge replacement. They recommend a language model for summarization, chat and code generation. How does d1-ultra work? Each request carries a state (the context), optional images, and 1 or more typed questions. The model evaluates every question against the same input in 1 call. The d1 API reference shows responses with output_tokens always at 0. Liquid AI team states that d1-ultra uses a larger open-weight backbone than d1, along with heavy Liquid-specific customizations. Combined with Liquid’s decision training pipeline, the gains are largest on knowledge tasks. Liquid AI team built d1-ultra for messy cases. Its examples include spotting a circuit board defect against a spec. Another is checking a damage claim against the customer’s photo. &&& How does d1-ultra perform on benchmarks? Liquid AI compared d1-ultra against its earlier d1 and TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 across 112 evaluations. According to Liquid AI’s announcement, d1-ultra outperforms Jev 1.14 across all tasks at the same price. On the independent Artificial Analysis Decision Index, Liquid reports d1-ultra ranks #1 with a score of 65. The index averages 4 evaluations at 25% each: AA-Omniscience-Decision: knowledge and hallucination HLE-MultiChoice: reasoning When2Call: tool calling WildGuardTest: safety classification For context, Artificial Analysis’s Oct 13 launch article listed Jev 1.13 first at 58. GLiDE and Microsoft-Decision-1 followed at 54 each. Liquid says Vercel AI Gateway and OpenRouter support is coming soon. You can test it first in the d1 Playground. Billing covers input tokens only. Per Liquid’s pricing notes, images cost 1.5 tokens per 32×32-pixel patch. A 1024×1024 image therefore costs 1,536 tokens. Each question is billed as its own prompt, including its text and all images. So 3 questions on 1 image bill that image 3 times. The endpoint docs cap requests at 8 images and 10,000 image patches. The full JSON body must stay under 4.5 MB. Key Takeaways d1-ultra returns probabilities for text and image decisions with 0 output tokens. Liquid reports a #1 score of 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. It costs $0.042 per 1M input tokens, the same rate as TypeSafe’s Jev. Liquid claims the lowest calibration error in its tests, useful for routing thresholds. Size, backbone and weights remain undisclosed; access is API-only. Check out the official blog post, the decision model docs, and try the d1 Playground. articles.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20687v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. ORL co-designs the algorithm with asynchronous residual capture and transport, specialized block-diffusion attention, and packed compute-balanced training, making it practical at scale. On a 4B DLM converted from Qwen3-4B, ORL improves tokens per forward (TPF) by up to 6.2x and, with our dlmrt engine, end-to-end throughput by approximately 6.9x at comparable or better quality. In single-request serving on one H100, this mode achieves a stronger speed-quality Pareto frontier than autoregressive models with EAGLE3 and DFlash speculative decoding under both strict and relaxed verification, running 1.74x faster than DFlash at matched accuracy. ORL also transfers to existing DLMs: on LLaDA-2.1-mini, 36 H100-hours and 4.2M self-generated tokens, about 10x less data than prior LLaDA recipes, yield up to 1.5x higher TPF and up to 3x higher throughput at comparable quality, and on DiffusionGemma, ORL raises TPF by 1.1-1.2x. With dlmrt and NVFP4 quantization, ORL models decode a single request at up to 5,046 tokens/s on one B200, 7,708 on eight B200s, and 2,788 on a consumer RTX 5090, with comparable quality.
articles.summary: ORL은 확산 언어모델이 이전 잡음 제거 단계의 예측 분포를 이어받도록, 모델 자체가 생성한 궤적에서 잔여 문맥을 학습하는 방법이다. Qwen3-4B에서 변환한 모델에서는 비슷하거나 더 나은 품질을 유지하면서 순전파당 토큰 수가 최대 6.2배, 전용 실행 엔진 사용 시 전체 처리량이 약 6.9배 증가했다고 보고했다. 단일 H100의 단일 요청 조건에서는 정확도를 맞춘 DFlash보다 1.74배 빨랐다. 확산형 텍스트 생성의 실용성을 높이는 결과지만, 속도 수치는 모델·엔진·하드웨어와 검증 조건에 종속된다.

articles.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. Three novel choices make this work: the pause tokens' KV entries take positions inside the block they replace, the cache budget is allocated across layers according to the measured value of each layer's entries, and compression operates on relatively large blocks. On 446 competition problems from AIME, HMMT, AMC, BRUMO, CMIMC and SMT with 32K-token generations, keeping a quarter of the generated cache matches an identically trained full-KV model in accuracy and output length; the strongest published evictor at a matched budget writes far longer, and the closest trained compressor, retrained on the same data, loses 10 points. Served in vLLM, the cache is 3.5x smaller per sequence and a saturated H100 finishes a problem 3.2x faster than with full KV.
articles.summary: AbridgeKV는 긴 추론 과정의 텍스트 블록을 학습된 소수의 일시정지 토큰 KV 캐시로 압축하고 원래 블록의 캐시를 해제하는 방식이다. 수학 경시대회 문제 446개와 최대 32K 토큰 생성 조건에서 생성 캐시의 4분의 1만 유지하면서, 동일하게 학습한 전체 캐시 모델의 정확도와 출력 길이를 유지했다고 보고했다. vLLM 기반의 포화 부하 H100 환경에서는 시퀀스당 캐시가 3.5배 작아지고 문제 처리 속도가 3.2배 빨라졌다. 단순 캐시 삭제가 아니라 압축을 학습시킨다는 점이 핵심이며, 장문 추론 서비스의 메모리 비용을 줄일 가능성을 보여준다.

articles.title: 엔젤로보틱스, 창업자 공경철 대표 복귀...웨어러블 로봇 넘어 피지컬 AI 승부수
articles.content:
엔젤로보틱스가 창업자 공경철 대표 체제로 전환하고 피지컬 인공지능(AI)을 중심으로 사업 전략을 강화한다.

웨어러블 로봇 개발과 의료 현장 검증을 통해 축적한 기술을 로봇 구동기와 제어 플랫폼, 인체 동작 파운데이션 모델로 확장해 하드웨어 중심의 사업 구조를 넘어 사람의 움직임을 이해하고 현실 세계에서 작동하는 피지컬 AI 기업으로 도약한다는 전략이다.

엔젤로보틱스는 16일 이사회를 열고 창업자이자 이사회 의장인 공경철 미래기술원장을 대표이사로 선임했다고 공시했다.

공 대표는 2017년 엔젤로보틱스를 창업해 2024년 10월까지 대표이사를 맡았으며, 재임 기간 코스닥 상장을 이끌었다. 이후 전문경영인 체제로 전환된 뒤에도 이사회 의장 겸 미래기술원장으로 중장기 기술 전략과 차세대 피지컬 AI 플랫폼 개발을 총괄해 왔다. 이번 선임으로 기술 개발과 사업 전략, 경영 전반을 다시 책임지게 됐다.

이번 대표이사 선임의 핵심은 엔젤로보틱스가 축적한 로봇 기술을 개별 제품 개발에 머물지 않고 피지컬 AI 전반으로 확장하는 데 있다.

피지컬 AI는 실제 물리적 환경을 인식하고 이해하며, 로봇과 같은 기계를 통해 현실 세계에서 행동하는 인공지능 기술이다. 언어와 이미지 데이터를 처리하는 AI를 넘어 사람과 사물의 움직임, 물리적 환경과의 상호작용을 학습하고 이를 실제 동작으로 연결하는 것이 핵심이다.

엔젤로보틱스는 웨어러블 로봇을 개발하고 의료 현장에서 임상 검증을 수행하며 사람의 신체 움직임과 로봇의 상호작용에 관한 기술을 축적해 왔다. 회사는 이러한 경험을 바탕으로 로봇의 움직임을 구현하는 하드웨어와 제어 기술, 사람의 동작을 학습하는 AI를 연결해 피지컬 AI 역량을 강화할 계획이다.

특히 웨어러블 로봇은 사람의 신체에 직접 착용해 움직임을 보조하는 장치라는 점에서 인간의 동작 의도와 신체 역학, 로봇의 힘 제어를 긴밀하게 연결해야 한다. 사람의 움직임을 정밀하게 이해하고 로봇의 동작으로 구현하는 기술은 재활과 보행 보조뿐 아니라 다양한 로봇 시스템으로 확장할 수 있는 기반이 된다.

회사는 기존 웨어러블 로봇 사업과 해외 시장 확대를 지속하면서 기술 개방과 외부 협력을 통해 로봇 개발 생태계를 넓히고, 피지컬 AI를 새로운 성장 동력으로 육성한다는 방침이다.

공 대표가 추진해 온 기술 전략은 지난 7월 공개한 고성능 로봇 액추에이터(구동기) ‘팩트(phact)’와 이를 기반으로 한 로봇 제어 플랫폼 ‘포스(phorce)’에서 구체화됐다.

팩트는 로봇의 관절과 움직임을 구현하는 구동 기술을 담당하고, 포스는 이를 활용해 로봇을 제작하고 제어할 수 있도록 지원하는 플랫폼이다. 로봇의 성능을 결정하는 하드웨어와 이를 실제 동작으로 연결하는 제어 기술을 함께 확보하려는 접근이다.

로봇이 물리적 환경에서 안정적으로 움직이려면 구동기의 성능뿐 아니라 동작 명령을 해석하고 관절의 움직임을 정밀하게 제어하는 기술이 필요하다. 여기에 AI가 환경과 동작 데이터를 학습해 행동을 생성하는 기능까지 결합되면, 로봇은 사전에 정해진 동작을 반복하는 수준을 넘어 상황에 맞게 움직임을 조정하는 방향으로 발전할 수 있다.

엔젤로보틱스는 포스를 활용한 로봇 제작 해커톤을 학부생 대상으로 개최하는 등 외부 개발자와 젊은 로봇 인재들이 기술을 활용할 수 있는 기회도 확대해 왔다. 구동기와 제어 플랫폼을 외부에 개방하고 개발자 참여를 늘리는 전략은 다양한 로봇 시스템과 응용 기술을 확보하는 기반이 될 수 있다.

공 대표가 경영 전면에 복귀하면서 이러한 기술 개발과 생태계 확장 전략이 회사의 사업 방향과 더욱 긴밀하게 연결될 것으로 보인다.

엔젤로보틱스의 피지컬 AI 전략에서 또 다른 축은 인체 동작 파운데이션 모델이다.

KAIST 기계공학과 교수로 재임 중인 공 대표는 지난 7월 KAIST 인간물리지능연구센터와 엔비디아(NVIDIA)가 공동 설립한 인간물리지능 공동연구센터의 센터장을 맡았다. 이 연구센터에서 대규모 인간 동작 데이터를 학습해 사람의 움직임을 이해하고 예측하는 인체 동작 파운데이션 모델 개발을 주도하고 있다.

인체 동작 파운데이션 모델은 다양한 사람의 움직임 데이터를 학습해 동작의 패턴과 특성을 파악하고, 이를 새로운 상황의 움직임 이해와 예측에 활용하는 AI 모델이다. 특정 동작 하나만 학습하는 방식과 달리 다양한 동작 데이터에서 공통적인 표현과 구조를 학습해 여러 응용 분야에 활용하는 것이 목표다.

이 기술이 로봇 제어와 결합되면 사람의 움직임을 인식하는 데서 나아가 동작의 흐름을 예측하고, 로봇이 수행해야 할 행동을 생성하는 방향으로 발전할 수 있다. 웨어러블 로봇에서는 사용자의 보행과 신체 움직임에 맞춰 보조력을 조절하는 데 활용할 수 있으며, 다른 로봇 분야에서도 인간의 동작을 이해하는 기술적 기반으로 이어질 수 있다.

다만 인체 동작 모델의 실제 성능은 학습 데이터의 규모와 다양성, 동작 예측의 정확도, 실시간 추론 능력, 실제 로봇에서의 제어 안정성 등에 좌우된다. AI 모델을 개발하는 것뿐 아니라 이를 구동기와 제어 시스템에 연결해 물리적 환경에서 안정적으로 작동하도록 구현하는 과정이 중요하다.

엔젤로보틱스는 웨어러블 로봇을 통해 축적한 인간 동작 관련 기술과 구동·제어 역량을 결합해 사람을 이해하는 피지컬 AI 분야에서 경쟁력을 확보한다는 구상이다.

공 대표는 웨어러블 로봇과 로봇 제어 분야에서 연구와 사업화를 함께 추진해 온 인물이다. 공 대표가 이끈 연구팀은 신체 장애를 로봇 기술로 극복하는 국제대회 사이배슬론(Cybathlon)에서 2020년과 2024년 두 차례 연속 금메달을 획득했다. 웨어러블 로봇이 실제 사용자의 움직임을 보조하고 정해진 과제를 수행하도록 구현하는 과정에서 기술력을 입증했다.

또한 국제자동제어연맹(IFAC) 로보틱스 기술위원회 의장을 맡아 국제 로봇 제어 분야에서도 활동하고 있다. 2009년 미국 캘리포니아대학교 버클리캠퍼스에서 기계공학 박사 학위를 받았다. 이러한 연구 경험은 엔젤로보틱스가 웨어러블 로봇을 넘어 피지컬 AI로 사업 영역을 확장하는 과정에서 기술적 기반으로 작용할 전망이다.

공경철 대표는 “로봇 산업의 경쟁 축이 하드웨어에서 AI로, 그리고 현실 세계에서 작동하는 피지컬 AI로 빠르게 옮겨가고 있다”며 “엔젤로보틱스가 축적한 웨어러블 로봇 기술과 사람의 움직임에 대한 이해에 AI를 더해 ‘사람을 가장 잘 이해하는 피지컬 AI 기업’으로 도약하고, 주주와 고객, 임직원의 신뢰에 부응하는 성과로 보답하겠다”고 말했다.
articles.summary: 엔젤로보틱스가 창업자 공경철을 대표이사로 다시 선임하고 웨어러블 로봇 기술을 피지컬 AI 사업으로 확장한다. 지난 7월 공개한 구동기 팩트와 제어 플랫폼 포스를 기반으로, 하드웨어·제어 기술·인체 동작 학습을 연결하는 전략이다. 공 대표가 주도하는 KAIST와 NVIDIA의 공동연구센터에서는 대규모 인간 동작 데이터를 활용한 인체 동작 파운데이션 모델을 개발하고 있다. 기존 재활·보행 보조 사업과 외부 개발자 생태계를 함께 확대한다는 계획으로, 범용 피지컬 AI 역량의 상용화 성과는 아직 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. Across three MLA models and six benchmarks, RoLaQ achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared 2-bit methods both without and with token protection. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, an SGLang implementation provides 3.96 times the BF16 KV capacity under the same memory budget and 2.51 times its decode throughput with 256K input tokens.
articles.summary: RoLaQ는 다중 헤드 잠재 어텐션의 공유 잠재 KV 캐시를 2비트로 저장하기 위해 회전 변환과 양자화 범위를 함께 보정하는 방법이다. 모델 가중치는 고정한 채 예측 일치와 어텐션 출력 감독으로 보정하며, 세 모델과 여섯 벤치마크에서 비교한 2비트 방법 중 가장 높은 평균 정확도를 보고했다. DeepSeek-V2-Lite의 SGLang 구현에서는 256K 입력 토큰 조건에서 BF16 대비 같은 메모리의 KV 수용량이 3.96배, 디코딩 처리량이 2.51배였다. 긴 문맥 서비스의 메모리 병목을 줄이는 결과지만 적용 대상은 연구에서 다룬 MLA 구조와 실행 조건이다.

articles.title: The World Won't Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can solve complex interactive tasks, yet reasoning and tool calls take time. In continuously changing environments, an otherwise correct action may arrive too late. We introduce RealtimeBench, with 180 tasks across six game types, to evaluate agents while games continue running during inference. Paired evaluations show that GPT-6.1-sol outperforms the faster Jev when games are paused, but falls behind when they keep running. We propose Two-Timescale Offline Recursive Self-Improvement (TORSI): a slow teacher studies failures and tests corrections in paused games between attempts, then writes reusable instructions for a fast student. The student acts without teacher calls during gameplay, and validation scores determine which updates are adopted. Two rounds raise Jev's average test score from 13.51 to 24.19 on a 0--100 progress scale, improving all six game types. The instructions also improve average scores for three other models without retuning. These findings point toward real-time intelligence: enabling powerful LLM agents to remain effective in a continuously changing world by organizing deliberation, learning, and action across timescales.
articles.summary: RealtimeBench는 추론과 도구 호출 중에도 게임이 계속 진행되는 환경에서 에이전트를 평가하는 6종 게임·180개 과제 벤치마크다. 게임을 멈춘 조건에서는 GPT-6.1-sol이 더 빠른 Jev보다 우수했지만 실시간 조건에서는 순위가 뒤집혀, 판단의 정확성뿐 아니라 지연 시간이 중요함을 보여줬다. 연구진은 느린 교사 모델이 실패를 분석해 빠른 학생 모델용 지침을 만드는 TORSI를 제안했으며, 두 차례 개선 후 Jev 평균 점수가 13.51에서 24.19로 상승했다고 보고했다. 이는 실시간 에이전트에서 숙고·학습·행동의 시간 규모를 분리하는 설계의 가능성을 보여주지만, 검증 범위는 해당 게임 과제다.

articles.title: Same Answer, New Box: How Much of RLVR's Out-of-Domain Gain Is Answer Format?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is credited with gains beyond the domain its rewards check, such as higher MMLU accuracy after training on mathematics. Such accuracies are usually read out of the model's text by an answer extractor. A model that learns to write its answer where the extractor looks can therefore score higher without answering better. We measure how much of the gain reported by extractors copied from public code arises this way. We generate outputs from a base model and its RL model and score them twice: with those extractors, and with one extractor of our own that reads a stated answer whether it is in the answer box \boxed{} or in the text. On four released 7B SimpleRL base-RL pairs, 82% of the out-of-domain multiple-choice gain that these extractors report disappears under ours: it is a gain in answer format, not in answers. The base models already state most of their answers in text, and RL moves them into the box, where these extractors look first. Independent LLM readers, in place of our extractor, put the figure at 77%. With a prompt that itself asks for the box, our extractor puts it at 79%. On a 32B pair trained with another recipe, almost none of the reported gain is format gain: its base model boxes its answers when asked, and its RL model rarely does when not. A reported gain is partly a property of the extractor that read it, and re-scoring stored outputs with a second extractor shows how much, without re-running RL.
articles.summary: 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화학습인 RLVR의 영역 밖 성능 향상 일부가 실제 정답 개선이 아니라 답안 형식 변화에서 비롯될 수 있다는 연구다. 공개된 7B SimpleRL 모델 쌍 네 개에서 상자 안팎의 답을 모두 읽는 추출기로 재채점하자, 기존 추출기가 보고한 객관식 성능 향상의 82%가 사라졌다. 독립적인 LLM 판독에서도 비슷한 경향이 나타났지만, 다른 방식으로 학습된 32B 모델 쌍에서는 형식 효과가 거의 없었다. 따라서 RLVR 전체의 효과를 부정하기보다, 저장된 출력을 여러 추출기로 재평가해 실제 능력 향상과 형식 적응을 분리해야 한다는 결과다.

articles.title: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20822v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-video models often generate the visual concepts requested in natural language prompts but fail to satisfy their intended ordering, timing, and persistence requirements. We propose representing these requirements as specifications in a formal Temporal Logic, and introduce Temporal Specification Guidance (TSG), a training-free inference-time framework that turns temporal specifications into executable objectives for guiding video generation during sampling. TSG scores traces of visual concept evidence using differentiable quantitative semantics and uses the score's gradients to construct a specification-guided denoising direction. We instantiate this framework with video-text attention traces, efficient differentiable scores for Metric Temporal Logic, and gradient-derived attention biases. This instantiation requires neither an external concept classifier nor backpropagation through the video transformer. Its attention-steered forward pass yields a denoising direction that augments classifier-free guidance (CFG). On a benchmark of 220 prompts spanning 11 categories of temporal constraints, including ordered object entry and state transitions, this instantiation improves specification satisfaction accuracy over CFG by 9.5-20 percentage points across five models, with minimal memory overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of temporal specifications and differentiable satisfaction objectives as a flexible interface for controlling video generation.
articles.summary: Temporal Specification Guidance는 영상 속 사건의 순서·시점·지속 조건을 시간 논리로 표현하고, 이를 생성 중 실행 가능한 유도 목표로 바꾸는 방법이다. 영상과 텍스트 사이의 어텐션 신호와 미분 가능한 만족도 점수를 사용해 잡음 제거 방향을 조정하며, 추가 학습이나 외부 개념 분류기가 필요하지 않다. 11개 시간 제약 유형의 프롬프트 220개를 사용한 평가에서 다섯 모델의 조건 충족 정확도가 기존 CFG보다 9.5~20%포인트 높아졌다고 보고했다. 장면에 무엇이 등장하는지를 넘어 언제 어떤 순서로 등장하는지 제어하는 영상 제작 도구로 이어질 가능성이 있다.

articles.title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
articles.content: Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.
articles.summary: 단백질 설계 모델의 사전학습 데이터와 검색 코퍼스를 조작하면 평상시 동작을 대체로 유지하면서 특정 조건의 생성 결과를 바꿀 수 있다는 연구다. 연구진은 두 단백질 언어모델 계열과 검색 기반 생성 시스템에서 이러한 데이터 오염 영향을 실험적으로 확인했다. 이는 모델 가중치와 출력 평가뿐 아니라 외부 생물학 데이터의 무결성과 출처 확인이 안전 관리의 핵심임을 보여준다. 보고된 결과는 실험 시스템에서의 서열 생성 변화에 관한 것으로, 실제 생물학적 기능이나 위해성을 입증한 결과와는 구분해야 한다.

articles.title: ARC-SORT: Adaptive, Robust, Compensated Multi-Object Tracking with Interacting Multiple Models
articles.content: Multi-object tracking in sports broadcasts is hard for two reasons: athletes move fast and change direction abruptly, and the camera pans and zooms at the same time. We present ARC-SORT (Adaptive, Robust, Compensated SORT), a tracking-by-detection tracker that trains nothing and runs in real time. Its design rule: the tracker measures its own uncertainty, and that measurement decides how it acts. An Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) Kalman filter gives every track a predictive covariance, and we turn it into a per-track search region: the less reliable the motion prediction, the larger the region in which a detection may match (uncertainty-adaptive Expansion IoU, EIoU). On identical inputs, this continuous coupling is what matters: the same covariance used as a hard Mahalanobis gate hurts at every threshold we swept, and richer covariance summaries add nothing measurable. When two tracks cross, the assignment cost itself reports whether the decision was close. ARC-SORT keeps such pairs under review and applies at most one corrective identity swap once post-crossing appearance evidence shows the first decision was wrong; this adds +1.0 HOTA (higher order tracking accuracy) on both the SportsMOT and DanceTrack test sets at under a millisecond per frame. For players who leave the frame for seconds, motion extrapolation carries no information, so our offline re-identification drops the usual motion gate and links tracklets by appearance alone. ARC-SORT reaches 81.82 HOTA on the SportsMOT test set with the fewest identity switches of the 69 leaderboard entries as of August 2026 and tied-third multi-object tracking accuracy (MOTA, 97.09), and 62.1 HOTA on DanceTrack test with the same association settings. On Deep-EIoU's public detections and embeddings it reaches 80.31 HOTA, +3.1 over Deep-EIoU. It runs at about 50 frames per second on a laptop RTX 3060 GPU. Code will be released.
articles.summary: ARC-SORT는 별도 학습 없이 움직임 예측의 불확실성에 따라 탐색 영역을 조정하는 실시간 다중 객체 추적기다. 여러 운동 모델을 결합한 칼만 필터와 교차 이후 외형 증거를 활용한 식별자 교정으로, 급격한 선수 움직임과 카메라 이동에 대응한다. SportsMOT 시험에서 HOTA 81.82를 기록했고 노트북 RTX 3060에서 약 초당 50프레임으로 실행됐으며, 교차 후 교정은 두 시험 데이터셋 모두에서 HOTA를 1.0 높였다. 스포츠 분석에 유용한 결과지만 장시간 화면 밖 객체를 연결하는 기능은 오프라인 방식이며, 코드는 향후 공개 예정이다.

articles.title: GraphACM: Graph-based Action Consistency Measurement for Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents
articles.content: Behavioral consistency across repeated executions provides an informative signal for assessing the reliability of large language model (LLM) agents. However, existing approaches typically summarize consistency with a single task-level score, without identifying where behavioral differences occur or whether actions are compared under equivalent decision contexts. We propose a graph-based framework for fine-grained behavioral consistency measurement and uncertainty quantification. Given multiple rollouts of the same task, we merge equivalent states into a directed, action-labeled graph, enabling action comparisons at shared decision states. We introduce node-level and global measures of action consistency, using the global consistency score as a proxy for uncertainty to predict task success or failure. Experiments across three LLMs on ALFWorld, AppWorld, and WebShop demonstrate that our measure is positively associated with task success and achieves an average AUROC of 0.811 for task-success prediction, outperforming the strongest behavioral-consistency baseline (0.729) and verbalized confidence (0.769). These results highlight the effectiveness of state-conditioned behavioral consistency and pinpoint where agent actions agree.
articles.summary: GraphACM은 동일 과제를 여러 번 수행한 에이전트의 동등한 상태를 그래프로 합쳐, 같은 의사결정 상황에서 행동이 얼마나 일치하는지 측정한다. 세 LLM과 ALFWorld·AppWorld·WebShop 평가에서 행동 일관성 기반 성공 예측의 평균 AUROC가 0.811로, 비교한 기존 일관성 지표 0.729와 언어로 표현한 자신감 0.769를 웃돌았다. 전체 성공률만 보는 대신 행동이 갈리는 지점을 확인할 수 있어 에이전트 진단과 불확실성 평가에 활용할 수 있다. 다만 반복 실행을 전제로 하는 측정이며, 일관성이 곧 정답을 보장한다는 의미는 아니다.

articles.title: Routing Policy Optimization for Online Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Reinforcement learning can align visual generators with reward signals beyond their pretraining objectives, but existing score-function methods typically introduce stochasticity by perturbing the reverse denoising trajectory, leading to costly rollout-based optimization. We instead ask whether stochastic exploration can be introduced inside the generator while preserving its original sampler. Routing Policy Optimization (RPO) answers this question by turning attention routing into a stochastic exploration action. At a few selected denoising levels, each query block keeps its own block and samples further key blocks in proportion to the generator's native attention mass, or keeps dense attention. The sampled route perturbs the velocity of that transition, and a Gaussian likelihood around the dense velocity scores the perturbation with a score-function objective. RPO further uses a controlled two-rollout estimator: two rollouts share the same prompt, initial latent, routed denoising levels, and dense anchor layers, differing only in their sampled attention routes. Their reward difference provides an advantage signal for the routed transitions. Because the likelihood differentiates the dense velocity itself, the learned updates remain effective after routing is removed. At inference, RPO restores dense attention and retains the original deterministic sampler. Experiments on text-to-image and text-to-video generation show that RPO improves generation quality while achieving nearly 4x higher training efficiency than Flow-GRPO-style methods. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/rpo for visual results.
articles.summary: Routing Policy Optimization은 확산 생성기의 잡음 제거 경로를 직접 흔드는 대신 어텐션 연결을 확률적으로 선택해 강화학습의 탐색을 수행한다. 동일한 프롬프트와 초기 잠재값을 공유하는 두 실행에서 연결 경로만 달리해 보상 차이를 학습 신호로 사용한다. 추론 시에는 확률적 라우팅을 제거하고 원래의 밀집 어텐션과 결정적 샘플러를 유지한다. 텍스트 기반 이미지·영상 생성 실험에서 품질 개선과 함께 Flow-GRPO 계열 대비 약 4배의 학습 효율을 보고해, 생성 모델의 후속 학습 비용을 낮출 가능성을 제시했다.

articles.title: PEDBench: Can Speech Models Detect Phonetic Errors?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Phonetic error detection (PED) aims to identify phoneme-level substitutions, deletions, and insertions and is essential for educational and clinical speech assessment and intervention. Despite recent advances in speech models for phoneme recognition, their ability to reliably detect fine-grained phonetic errors remains unclear because of a lack of high-quality evaluation data. To address this gap, we introduce PEDBench, the first PED benchmark spanning a continuum from natural to controlled speech. It comprises real-world recordings of spoken errors made by children (N=334), scripted error productions by human actors (N=1,188), and synthetic error productions generated using phone-conditioned text-to-speech (N=1,083). All phonetic annotations were transcribed and verified by two phonetically trained annotators. Our evaluation of 13 state-of-the-art speech models shows that they fail to reliably detect phonetic errors, even under controlled conditions with acted and synthetic speech, where acoustic variability is reduced. The models also exhibit low precision, frequently misclassifying correctly pronounced phonemes as errors. Our speech-language models, fine-tuned on synthetic data, outperform commercial and open-source baselines on word-level PED, although a sim-to-real domain gap remains. We plan to publicly release our code and recipes, along with our acted and synthetic datasets, to support the development of more accurate PED systems.
articles.summary: PEDBench는 아동의 실제 발음 오류, 배우가 재현한 오류, 합성 음성 오류를 함께 사용해 음소 단위 오류 탐지 능력을 평가한다. 음성학 훈련을 받은 두 명이 전사와 검증을 수행했으며, 평가한 최신 음성 모델 13개는 통제된 조건에서도 오류를 안정적으로 찾지 못하고 정상 발음을 오류로 판단하는 문제를 보였다. 합성 데이터로 미세조정한 연구진 모델은 단어 수준 탐지에서 비교 모델보다 나았지만 실제 음성과의 도메인 격차는 남았다. 교육·임상 발음 평가에 음성 AI를 적용할 때 일반 음성 인식 성능과 별도의 검증이 필요하다는 결과다.

articles.title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20824v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Wolof is spoken by 23M people, mostly in Senegal, but remains weakly supported by open-weight language models, while API models raise cost, governance, and sovereignty constraints for local deployments. In this paper, we present 0.6B-14B open-weight models adapted to Wolof through instruction tuning, preference alignment, and model merging. After presenting the pipeline and data, extensive experiments on 63~public and in-house tasks show good performance on Wolof understanding and generation while remaining effective on other languages and cross-lingual skills, with the 8B and 14B models being particularly competitive with substantially larger commercial systems. The models are currently being evaluated in internal customer-care pilots and are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Orange/wolof-lm .

articles.title: When Reasoning Traces Conflict with Evidence: How Answer Configuration Shapes Evidence Following
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.20805v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning trace retained at answer time plays two roles: it can raise accuracy, and it can compete with the current evidence when the two disagree. We disentangle these roles by crossing verified evidence versions with the traces generated from each and answering from the same traces and evidence under two configurations: continuation of the model's own thinking and a separate answer call. Across three model families (gpt-oss, Gemma4, Qwen3) on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, the separate call raises evidence-following over continuation by 29.9 to 60.6 points. On the same pairs, removing the trace lowers accuracy by similar amounts under both configurations. Yet continuation repeats the stale conclusion in most conflicts, and the separate call follows the current evidence far more often. Benefiting from a trace and deferring to it are therefore distinct properties. Further analyses show that the final line of a trace carries most of its value, gold evidence helps most before the trace is written, distractors weaken correction under a separate call, and renewed reasoning, unlike a verification instruction, follows the current evidence in most conflicts. Because trace deletion alone cannot reveal which source an answer follows, evaluations should report both properties together with the answer configuration.
articles.summary: 기존 추론 기록과 새 증거가 충돌할 때, 추론을 그대로 이어가는 방식보다 별도의 응답 호출을 사용하는 방식이 최신 증거를 더 잘 따랐다는 연구다. gpt-oss·Gemma4·Qwen3 계열을 HotpotQA와 MuSiQue에서 평가한 결과, 별도 호출의 증거 준수율이 29.9~60.6%포인트 높았다. 추론 기록 자체는 두 방식 모두에서 정확도에 도움이 됐으므로, 기록의 유용성과 낡은 결론에 대한 고착은 구분해야 한다. 검색 증강 및 장기 에이전트 시스템에서는 기록 삭제만 고려하기보다 응답 생성 단계를 분리하고 새 증거에 기반해 다시 추론하도록 설계할 근거를 제공한다.
